pages.title: Teacup Town Weather Window Exhibit Clues
pages.notebookSkill: turning one exhibit clue into a weather detail
pages.visitFit: 15-minute adult-led museum or gallery table page for younger writers after a quiet look at one color, shape, pattern, or display object.
pages.adultSetup: Print the page, set out pencils, invite one quiet sketch from a pretend exhibit clue, and keep the writing at the table.
pages.kidDirection: Choose one color or shape from a display, turn it into teacup weather, and write what the tiny helper notices.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask, "Which exhibit clue could become weather in Teacup Town?" Then model one short because sentence.

pageSections.heading: Exhibit Clue
lines: The exhibit clue I noticed was a color: ____________________.
The display object shape looked like ____________________.
The quiet sketch on my page shows ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Weather Window
lines: In Teacup Town, that clue turns into weather called ____________________.
The spoon-shaped window fogs up with ____________________.
The tiny room corner changes when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny Story Note
lines: First, the weather watcher points to ____________________.
Next, the helper writes a label that says ____________________.
My museum-day story sentence is ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share line: One exhibit clue I turned into weather was ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: Wrap-up line: The detail that made my teacup scene clearer was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Skip sharing and finish this quiet sketch label: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: At home, add one new color clue for Teacup Town: ____________________.

pages.title: Spoon Ferry Lunchbox Harbor Display Log
pages.notebookSkill: using a display object to build a setting
pages.visitFit: 18-minute adult-led field-trip table page for turning one invented museum observation into a harbor setting.
pages.adultSetup: Print the page, choose a nearby display color or shape as a shared example, and remind writers to invent all places and labels.
pages.kidDirection: Pick one display object clue, imagine it as harbor cargo, and write a short ferry log.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which object, color, or pattern could belong on a tiny spoon ferry, then help writers add one setting word.

pageSections.heading: Display Object
lines: The display object I choose has this shape: ____________________.
The label clue I can invent for it says ____________________.
A pattern on the object reminds me of ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Lunchbox Harbor
lines: The spoon ferry docks beside a harbor corner with ____________________.
The cargo on the ferry is ____________________.
The lunchbox map marks the route with ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Log
lines: First, the ferry helper checks the clue called ____________________.
Next, the harbor display glows with the color ____________________.
The ferry log ending says ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share line: The museum object clue I used for harbor cargo was ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: Wrap-up line: The setting detail I can picture best is ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Draw the route silently, then add this map word: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one new display object to the ferry log: ____________________.

pages.title: Pocket Park Notice Board Label Notes
pages.notebookSkill: turning a label clue into a message and reason
pages.visitFit: 18-minute adult-led museum table activity for writers who can invent a notice from a color, map, pattern, or label.
pages.adultSetup: Print the page, point to one general label style without copying specific wording, and keep every notice fictional.
pages.kidDirection: Choose an exhibit clue, invent a pocket park notice, and explain why the helper posts it.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask, "What could this label remind a tiny park helper to do?" Then guide one because line.

pageSections.heading: Label Clue
lines: The invented label clue begins with the word ____________________.
The color on the display makes me think of ____________________.
The pattern I noticed looks like ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Pocket Park Notice
lines: The first pocket park notice asks for ____________________.
The notice board map points toward ____________________.
The quiet room corner becomes a park spot called ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Reason Note
lines: This notice helps because ____________________.
The pocket park helper carries ____________________.
The final message on the board says ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share line: The notice I can read from my notebook is ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: Wrap-up line: The reason that made my notice clear was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Copy one notice quietly here: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one home observation that could become a pocket park notice: ____________________.

pages.title: Button Bakery Map Mix-Up Gallery Route
pages.notebookSkill: turning map observations into clear story directions
pages.visitFit: 20-minute adult-led gallery or museum table page for using one invented map clue and three clear route steps.
pages.adultSetup: Print the page, offer beside, around, past, and near as direction words, and keep the route on paper only.
pages.kidDirection: Choose a map, shape, or display clue, imagine it as a bakery route, and fix the mixed-up directions.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask writers to replace a vague route with one object, one color, and one direction word from their observation.

pageSections.heading: Gallery Map Clue
lines: The museum map clue I noticed looks like ____________________.
The shape that could become a bakery path is ____________________.
The color tab on my pretend route is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Bakery Mix-Up
lines: The crumb path points the wrong way toward ____________________.
The button baker checks a display object shaped like ____________________.
The mixed-up label says to stop near ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Fixed Directions
lines: First, follow the map past ____________________.
Next, turn around the bakery pattern called ____________________.
The fixed route ends beside ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share line: The route clue I can share from my map is ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: Wrap-up line: The direction word that helped my story was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Trace the route silently, then finish this bakery clue: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one new map clue for the Button Bakery route: ____________________.

pages.title: Penny Path Compass Shop Observation Card
pages.notebookSkill: using observation words to write a compass route
pages.visitFit: 20-minute adult-led museum-day notebook page for turning quiet sketch details into a simple compass-shop route.
pages.adultSetup: Print the page, place pencils at the table, invite one color, shape, map, or label observation, and keep sharing optional.
pages.kidDirection: Pick one observation clue, pretend it points a compass, and write three directions for Penny Path.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which clue would point north, south, east, or west in a pretend compass shop, then help choose one route detail.

pageSections.heading: Penny Path Route
